MEMORANDUM

  Agenda Item #: __8___
  Meeting Date: March 27, 2018

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

THRU:  ANTON DAHLERBRUCH, CITY MANAGER /s/

FROM:  SHERI REPP-LOADSMAN, DEPUTY CITY MANAGER/PLANNING
  & BUILDING DIRECTOR /s/

SUBJECT: CONSIDERATION OF PARKLANDS COMMITTEE
  RECOMMENDATIONS OF MARCH 8, 2018

DATE:  MARCH 27, 2018

ISSUE/PURPOSE

The purpose of this memorandum is to transmit Parklands Committee recommendations from
the March 8, 2018 meeting to the City Council.

BACKGROUND/DISCUSSION

At its meeting of March 8, 2018 the Parklands Committee reviewed and discussed 7
applications for tree removals, one applications in Parklands for retention of private plantings,
one application for a topping of trees, 2 application for a waiver of planting of the Designated
Street Tree and one Final Plan for a Change To Parklands as follows:

1. PC-494-18; Application to remove 1 Chinese Flame tree located in the parkway adjacent to
  2837 Via Segovia

  Applicant:  Jim and Carol McKay
  2837 Via Segovia
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  Page 1 of 6

  001
   The applicant summarized past issues with the sewer due to the tree roots. Chairman Wade
  noted the 2012 invoice and asked questions related to the lining of the sewer. The applicant’s
  plumber testified that the sewer is starting to lift in spots and there is root intrusion near the
  connection with the main line. The Committee noted there might be a potential safety risk and
  the subject tree was not the designated street tree or contributory to neighborhood character.

  Action: Committee member Leach motioned second by Kaviani to recommend to the City
  Council approval of PC-494-18 according to the ‘Standard Conditions for Tree Removal
  Approvals’. Payment of $500 to the ‘Tree Bank’ and removal of the stump are required. The
  vote was (4-0-1 in favor, Rubincam absent).

  2. PC-495-18; Application to remove 1 Italian Stone pine tree located in the parkway
  adjacent to 2525 Via Amador

  Applicant:  Anthony Bailey
  2524 Via Rivera
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  The applicant explained the reasons for requesting removal of the Stone pine tree and interest
  in keeping the adjacent Olive tree. The Parklands Committee noted that the tree does constitute
  a major view obstruction and removal would not adversely affect the neighborhood character.

  Action: Committee member Kaviani motioned second by Leach to recommend to the City
  Council approval of PC-495-18 according to the ‘Standard Conditions for Tree Removal
  Approvals’. Payment of $500 to the ‘Tree Bank’ and removal of the stump are required. The
  vote was (3-0-1-1 in favor, Rubincam absent, Richie-Bray recused).

3.  PC-496-18; Application to consider either a Magnolia or Olive tree as the alternative
  ‘Designated Street Tree’ for the parkway adjacent to 2217 Via Guadalana

  Applicant:  Robert Bell
  2217 Via Guadalana
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  The applicant requested that the Parklands Committee consider an alternate designated street
  tree to be planted in the parkway in front of his home explaining that three large Eucalyptus
  were recently allowed to be removed for view enhancement. The applicant further noted that
  the resident authorized to remove the trees had expressed to him that the tree removal did not
  help the view. There was discussion of the Western Red Bud as the designated street tree and
  the interest to have Magnolia or Olive trees as an alternate choice. Chairman Wade questioned
  if the alternate tree discussion should apply to the entire street. The Committee discussed the
  ability to make a determination on the designated street tree for a specific property or the entire
  street acknowledging that public notice had been provided for the subject property. There was
  discussion of the street containing many different species and the Western Red Bud not being
  planted on many properties in the area. The Committee determined that the Little Gem
  Magnolia would be small and not expected to impact views.

  Page 2 of 6

  002
 Action: Committee member Richie-Bray motioned second by Kaviani to recommend to the City
Council approval of PC-496-18 to allow the Little Gem Magnolia to be the ‘Designated Street
Tree’ adjacent to 2217 Via Guadalana. Two Little Gem Magnolia trees are approved to be
planted by the City. The vote was (3-1-1 in favor, Wade opposed and Rubincam absent).

Subsequent to the Parklands Committee meeting, on March 11, 2018, Chairman Wade provided
written correspondence for consideration related to this item.

It is staff’s understanding that the correspondence from Parklands Chairperson Bob Wade
regarding PC-496-18 is intended to identify the broader policy issue that may be associated
with this application. Specifically, the issue is how the Parklands Committee should handle an
individual’s request to plant a tree that isn’t the designated street tree. In addition, the
correspondence is intended to insure that the City Council has all the information to make an
informed decision.

The policy issue is the manner in which a designated street tree is approved. In PC-496-18, it
is being addressed by an individual application and requests that an alternate designated street
tree be approved for the subject property. The issue here is not solely about this tree; the issue
to consider is whether a precedent is being created by affirming the Parkland Committee
recommendation and for the Parklands Committee to receive direction for future applications.
It is important to know in this regard that requests like this have been received and approved
by the City Council, however they are infrequent. There is no pattern or precedent that has
been created.

The City routinely reviews and updates the list of approved trees that may be planted on public
streets. The Designated Street Tree List represents carefully selected tree species that are
appropriate to our climate and take into account views, neighborhood character, maintenance
and resistance to insects and disease. During the review of the Tree Management Policy, both
the Parklands Committee and the City Council discussed the potential for alternate tree species
to be designated in recognition of an existing or desirable character achieved by the public trees.
The policy question focuses on the ability for an alternative designated street tree to be
identified for a street or an individual property. Although the application was properly noticed
and posted for the subject property, there was not a separate, specified agenda discussion for
re-considering the designated tree for the street.

We understand that the Parklands Chairperson is not directly asking to have PC-496-18
removed from the Consent Agenda. The point is to receive direction for the Parklands
Committee. Four options are before the City Council in reference to this application:

1. As recommended by the Parklands Committee, the City Council approve the application.
2. As recommended by the Parklands Committee, the City Council approve the application
  and direct staff to add this policy matter onto an agenda for a joint meeting of the Parklands
  Committee and City Council.
3. The City Council remand PC-496-18 to Parklands for a discussion of the designated street
  tree for the entire street. Note: the Parklands Committee would meet in May to discuss the
  street tree and reconsider PC-496-18. If completed in one Parklands Committee meeting,
  the application would return to the City Council for approval in June.
4. Other action as deemed appropriate.

  Page 3 of 6

  003
 Either alternative #2 or #3 above would address Chair Wade’s interest. The Council may also
chose alternative #1 by approving this item on the Consent Agenda. At this time, it is also not
recommended that the City Council remove this Consent Agenda item for discussing the policy
of street trees, as the policy is not listed for discussion on the City Council agenda.

4. PC-497-18; Application to remove 6 Carob trees located in the parkways adjacent to 415,
424 and 500 Paseo Del Mar, and 1 Carob tree located in the  parkway adjacent to 501 Via
Media

  Applicant:  Janine Nendick
  508 Via Media
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Action: Committee member Wade motioned second by Leach to recommend to the City Council
approval of PC-497-18 according to the ‘Standard Conditions for Tree Removal Approvals’.
Reduce by topping the 3 Carob trees located in the parkway adjacent to 500 Paseo Del Mar and
the 1 Carob tree located in the parkway adjacent to 424 Paseo Del Mar to 25 feet in height.
Standard trimming of the Carob tree located in the parkway adjacent to 415 Paseo Del Mar is
approved. Payment of $500 and removal of the stump are required. The vote was (4-0-1 in
favor, Rubincam absent).

Subsequent to the Parklands Committee meeting, an appeal was received from Mrs. Pat Vancura
requesting City Council review of the application. The appeal is tentatively scheduled for May
8, 2018. As such, the City Council will not take action on PC-497-18 at this time.

5. PC-498-18; Application to remove, top or trim 6 trees located in La Costa Lane East
adjacent to 2836/2844 Palos Verdes Drive West and 2 trees in the Parklands adjacent to 809
Tyburn Road

  Applicant;  Justin and Elisa Yaros
  2805 Via Rivera
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

The applicant advised that the remodel of their home and backyard was nearing completion and
the request to remove the trees was to enhance ocean views. The Committee discussed the
various condition of the trees. There was discussion of the location of the trees in areas behind
homes and that, in some cases, the adjoining residents had moved fences to incorporate the
public land into the rear yards without authorization. The Ash and Silver Oak trees were noted
as being significant trees to the neighborhood.

Action: Committee member Richie-Bray motioned second by Kaviani to recommend to the City
Council approval of PC-498-18, with modification. Approve removal of the 1 Eucalyptus tree,
2 Ash trees and 1 Ficus tree located in La Costa Lane East adjacent to 2836 Palos Verdes Drive
West according to the ‘Standard Conditions for Tree Removal Approvals’. Approve standard
trimming of 2 Ash trees located on La Costa Lane East adjacent to 2844 Palos Verdes Drive
West and topping to the previous cuts of 1 Ash tree located in the Parklands adjacent to 809

  Page 4 of 6

  004
 Tyburn Road. Standard trimming of 1 Silk Oak is approved. Payment of $2,000 and removal
of the stumps are required. The vote was (3-0-1-1 in favor, Rubincam absent, Leach recused).

6. PC-499-18; Application for a Native Restoration Plan located in the Parklands  adjacent
to 1405 Via Montemar

  Applicant:  Miriam Rainville Design Studio
  1632 Aviation Boulevard
  Redondo Beach, CA 90278

The applicant’s representative summarized the request for a native restoration plan and agreed
that the area would be extended to address the entire disturbed area. A resident shared concern
related to the prior unauthorized grading by the applicant that caused damage to the parklands
and requested only low growing plants be approved. She also noted easement had been blocked
and should be restored. The Committee discussed the condition of the parklands area and need
for restoration.

Action: Committee member Richie-Bray motioned second by Wade to recommend to the City
Council approval of PC-499-18, with conditions. Approval of a revised after the fact grading
plan to return the Parklands to the previous grade, modify the plan to add Lemonade Berry,
Ribes and Encelia, restore the entire Parklands as determined by staff by field measurements,
install a specimen 60-inch box Aleppo pine approved by the Urban Forester and pay a
restoration fee for the damaged Aleppo pine as determined by the Planning Director. The vote
was (4-0-1 in favor, Rubincam absent).

7. PC-500-18; Application to remove 4 Hollywood Junipers located in the parkway adjacent
to 1421 Via Zumaya

  Applicant:  William Epstein
  1424 Via Zumaya
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

The applicant noted that the property owner responsible for the Junipers had provided some
trimming to demonstrate the potential for the views to be restored. The applicant noted the
height was still an impact. A resident requested that the unauthorized Junipers be removed and
another resident supported trimming. The impacted property owner, Mrs. Strum, requested
authorization to trim and shape the Junipers. There was discussion of the significant view
impacts and the difficulty in providing trimming since they were so overgrown.

Action: Committee member Kaviani motioned second by Leach to recommend to the City
Council approval of PC-500-18 according to the ‘Standard Conditions for Tree Removal
Approvals’. Payment of $2,000 to the ‘Tree Bank’ and removal of the stumps are required. The
vote was (4-0-1 in favor, Rubincam absent).

  Page 5 of 6

  005
 RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council take the following actions:

1. Review and approve the Parklands Committee Recommended Actions of March 8, 2018.

B - Staff report for PC-495-18
C - Staff report for PC-496-18
D - Staff report for PC-498-18
E - Staff report for PC-499-18
F - Staff report for PC-500-18
G: Correspondence from Chairman Wade dated March 11, 2018

  Page 6 of 6

  006
   Attachment G
Lauren Pettit

To:  Anton Dahlerbruch
Subject:  RE: Parklands Committee - PC-496-18 (Robert Bell)

From: Bob Wade [mailto:  ]
Sent: Sunday, March 11, 2018 2:25 PM
To: Anton Dahlerbruch <adahlerbruch@pvestates.org>
Cc: Sheri Repp <srepp@pvestates.org>
Subject: Parklands Committee ‐ PC‐496‐18 (Robert Bell)

Tony-
Please provide copies of this email to the City Council in advance of the March 27th meeting. Thanks.

**************************************

Mayor Vandever and Members of the City Council-

At the recent Parklands Committee meeting on March 8th, the above-referenced application was considered and voted
upon. My understanding is that the matter will be on the agenda for consideration by the City Council on March 27th.

In PC-496-18, the applicant Robert Bell requested that the Committee approve the planting of trees other than the
designated street tree (DST) in the parkway area of his property fronting Via Guadalana. Mr. Bell was seeking to
plant new trees to improve the appearance of his property, as the Committee had approved the removal of three large
Eucalyptus trees from his parkway area in a previous view enhancement case. Mr. Bell was of the opinion that the
current DST for Via Guadalana (the Western Redbud) is not attractive for a significant portion of the year and would
not enhance the appearance of his property. His request was for the Committee to approve the planting of either olive
or magnolia trees in his parkway in lieu of the Western Rosebud.

The Committee members all agreed that the Little Gem Magnolia would be attractive, view-sensitive and appropriate
as an alternative street tree. However, there was a lack of unanimity on the issue of whether it is appropriate for the
Committee to approve an alternative street tree at the request of an individual property owner as opposed to a more
formal process of notifying the residents on the street of a proposal to either change the DST or provide an
alternative. Ultimately, the Committee voted 3-1 (one member absent) to approve the applicant’s request. I was the
dissenting vote, for the following reasons:

  1. Approving alternative DST’s for a residence at the request of an individual applicant would set an
  adverse precedent. Other residents could be encouraged to submit similar applications for DST’s that
  they prefer, thereby potentially undermining the integrity of the City’s street tree program.
  2. The past practice in designating a new or alternate DST has been to notice residents on the street of such
  a proposal for consideration at a subsequent Parklands Committee meeting. I am aware of only one
  possible variation of this practice in the case of an application concerning 1812 Paseo Del Mar (PC-474-
  17), decided by the Committee on September 14, 2017. In that case, the applicant agreed to plant DST’s
  (the Kentia Palm) in the curb area of the parkway. The parkway setback on the property is quite large,
  extending nearly 40 feet back from the street to within three feet of the circular driveway. In that case,
  the Committee approved the planting of three Eastern Rosebuds 25 feet back from the street to provide
  shade and privacy to the resident. The integrity of the DST program was still maintained, while
  providing reasonable relief for the applicant to improve the appearance and enjoyment of his
  property. That Paseo Del Mar case is clearly distinguishable from the case at hand, in my opinion.

  1  007
 In my view, the proper procedure in the Bell case would have been to continue the matter to the next Parklands
Committee meeting and, in the interim, provide appropriate notification to residents on Via Guadalana of the proposal
to designate the Little Gem Magnolia as an alternative DST. I realize that there is inconvenience to the applicant,
delay and added complexity by doing so. However, I do think those concerns are off-set by avoiding adverse
precedent that risks undermining the integrity of the DST program. I also believe the other residents on the street
deserve due process through notification and an opportunity to be heard on a matter affecting their neighborhood.

In your consideration of PC-496-18 at the March 27th meeting, I would appreciate Council providing guidance to the
Parklands Committee in cases where residents apply for planting of trees other than the applicable DST in the
parkway abutting their property. More specifically, I think the Committee needs guidance on whether the Committee
can or should approve such requests, and, if so, under what circumstances. Secondly, in such cases, should other
residents on the street be given notice and an opportunity to be heard.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,

Bob Wade, Parklands Chairman

  2  008
